name: trackeros
description:
Trackeros — a corporate operations web and mobile platform for
  mid-sized companies. Provides employee self-service (leave
  requests, balances, expense claims), manager workflows
  (approvals, team views, time-off calendars), and HR admin
  surfaces (leave policy configuration, balance accruals,
  audit reports).
  
  Backend: TypeScript on Node 20 (Fastify), PostgreSQL via
  Knex migrations + a thin repository layer, BullMQ for
  background jobs (accrual schedulers, notification fanout).
  Module structure: src/modules/<name>/<name>.{model,
  repository,service,controller,routes}.ts. Domain modules
  include leave, balance, employee, policy, notification.
  Shared utilities under src/shared/ (db connection, base
  repository, error types).
  
  Frontend: React + Vite SPA for the web client, React Native
  for the mobile client (shared @trackeros/contracts package
  for the typed REST surface). Auth via JWT against the
  backend's /auth endpoints; identity comes from corporate
  OIDC in production and from local users in development.
  
  Tests: Jest for unit + integration. CI on GitHub Actions
  runs lint (ESLint) + typecheck (tsc --noEmit) + unit tests +
  a Semgrep security pass on every PR. Conventional Commits +
  squash-merge. Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict
  null checks).
_comment_gate: qualityGate: what the gate enforces. `applicationRoots` declares each BUILD in this repository so the dependency map in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md can describe more than one; `ownedDecisions` names symbols whose rule belongs to a single module. Both are read by the constraint agent's deterministic checks. See docs/guides/pipeline-yaml.md.

qualityGate._comment_applicationRoots: Each BUILD whose module boundaries the dependency map describes. `prefix` keeps two builds' identically-named modules apart in one flat map; `containers` are the directories under the root that hold modules. Module names DERIVE from the path: <prefix><name> under `modules`, <prefix><container>-<name> elsewhere. Declare nothing and only the repository-root src/ is checked. The web/src root is declared because this template targets a web front end; a root that matches no directory yet is inert until the project creates one.
qualityGate._comment_ownedDecisions: Symbols whose meaning is a POLICY, and the modules allowed to branch on them. A rule expressed in two places eventually gets expressed inconsistently. Flags COMPARISONS only — a type annotation or an import is a reference, not a decision — and only on lines the phase wrote. Declare nothing and the check does nothing. Empty here because the symbols are a PROJECT's own: add a row per policy type, e.g. {"symbol": "<Role enum>", "owners": ["<module that owns the rule>"], "why": "..."}.

constraints._comment: Project-wide rules. Every rule MUST name its enforcer — a rule that names none is policy nobody applies, which is the state all four of these were in until 2026-09-30. `ci` rules name a job in this project's own workflows; the gate CONFIRMS that job ran rather than re-checking, because re-implementing semgrep or eslint beside them would be strictly worse and would double every finding.

rules.description: Use unknown with type guards instead of any
No hardcoded passwords, API keys, or tokens

_comment_verification: verification.command: the project's REAL install+compile+test invocation, run in the work dir after the code agent declares done and BEFORE the commit, so a compile error cannot reach CI. Ideally the same command CI runs. Absent or empty means verification is skipped.

verification.command: npm install --include=dev --no-audit --no-fund && if find src -name '*.ts' -not -name '*.spec.ts' -not -name '*.test.ts' -not -name '*.d.ts' -type f | grep -q .; then npm run build && npx jest --passWithNoTests --forceExit && npm run smoke; else echo 'no source files to verify'; fi
